dupehound is a multi-language static analysis tool for detecting code duplication (type-1, type-2, and type-3 clones).
It uses a token-based sliding window algorithm with FNV-64a hashing. The core packages are:
  - services/tokenizer.go  — lexer that normalizes source into token streams
  - services/detector.go   — sliding window hash + maximal block merge algorithm
  - services/scanner.go    — file walking, language detection, orchestration
  - services/reporter.go   — text/JSON/SARIF output formatting

Focus your review on:
  - Correctness of clone detection logic (false positives, false negatives, edge cases)
  - Lexer correctness (comment stripping, string literal handling, keyword disambiguation)
  - Performance regressions in hot paths (hashing, indexing, window sweeping)
  - Exit code contract: exit 1 = clones found, exit 2 = tool error, exit 0 = clean
  - Test coverage gaps — missing edge cases in tokenizer or detector
  - Off-by-one errors in line range reporting (StartLine/EndLine accuracy)
  - Concurrency safety if any goroutines are introduced
  - Error wrapping — errors should use %w so callers can use errors.Is

Do NOT comment on:
  - Minor naming style preferences
  - Reordering of import groups (gofumpt handles this)
  - Adding comments to self-evident code
  - Whitespace or formatting (gofumpt handles this)
